41.61,-76.12: Sullivan's March. Gen. John Sullivan's army camped on the lowland here Aug. 4, 1779. The fourth encampment between Fort Wyoming and Tioga Point.

Sullivan Expedition Against the Iroquois Indians, 1779 - Vanderlip's Farm (PLAQUE). Fourteen miles from Tunkhannock, Fourth Encampment of Sullivan's Army, on the march from Wyoming to Teaoga August 4-5, 1779, lay on this lowland known as blade Walnut Flats.
41.72,-76.29: Joseph Elliot - PLAQUE. Second in command at the Battle of Lime Hill April 14, 1782. He killed the Indian who shot Mrs. Franklin and rescued three of her four stolen children. He was in the engagement at Trenton December 25, 1776 and was presented with a sword by General George...
41.74137,-76.33902: Sullivan Expedition Against the Iroquois Indians, 1779 - Standing Stone (PLAQUE). 9 1/2 miles from Wyalusing, sixth encampement of Sullivan's army on the march from Wyoming to Teaoga August 8-9, 1779, was on river lowlands opposite the Standing Stone.
41.75,-76.32: Sullivan's March. Gen. John Sullivan's army camped on the nearby river lowlands Aug. 8-9, 1779 en route to attack the Six Nations Iroquois. Sixth camp between Wyoming and Fort Sullivan.
41.77,-76.44: Stephen Foster. The great writer of folk songs and ballads lived in Towanda in 1840-41. He attended Towanda Academy on the hill a short time and stayed with his brother William, a canal official.

Bradford County. Formed on February 21, 1810 from Lycoming and Luzerne counties. Named Ontario County until 1812; renamed for the second U.S. Attorney General, William Bradford. County seat of Towanda was incorporated 1828. Famous for Sullivan's March and David Wilmot.
41.77,-76.45: David Wilmot. The great Free-Soiler, who began the fight on slavery extension with the Wilmot Proviso in 1846, lived in this house. Republican Party founder; its first candidate for Governor. He died here in 1868.
41.8,-76.38: Lester Frank Ward. "Father of American Sociology," geologist, and Civil War veteran, L.F. Ward (1841-1913), spent his youth in Myersburg working with his brother, Cyrenus Osborne Ward, labor historian, in their hub factory. He has been called "the American Aristotle."
41.86,-76.34: Philip P. Bliss. The great singing evangelist and gospel song writer lived and taught school at one time in Bradford County. The cemetery monument was built by Sunday School gifts from England and U.S. after his death in 1876.
